packets.responsibility: Applies an affine matrix `m` to one raw stroke-data dict's OWN geometry, dispatching on `sd.isRaster`. Raster branch (lines 1330-1345): translates the center (`sd.x`,`sd.y`) by the full affine, and scales `width`/`height` by the matrix's own per-axis linear magnitude (`scaleX=\sqrt(a²+b²)`, `scaleY=\sqrt(c²+d²)`) — a rotate component of `m` degrades to scale-only for a raster, matching the persisted raster schema's real capability (no rotation field; see serR/desR, C21e, cited by name only). ONLY `x`,`y`,`width`,`height` are transformed; `src`,`opacity` are copied through unchanged, and every other optional raster tag (isBitmapBrush, linked/linkedPath/linkedHandleId, rotation, brushGroupId, isBrushTextureCopy, meshId, groupId, the text-tool fields) is DROPPED — the returned dict for a raster branch is a fresh literal listing only the six named keys, not a copy-and-patch of `sd`. Vector branch (lines 1346-1358): early-returns `sd` unchanged if it has no `segments`; otherwise MUTATES `sd.segments` IN PLACE (line 1347's `sd.segments=sd.segments.map(...)` reassigns the same object's own field) — every segment's `point` gets the FULL affine; `handleIn`/`handleOut` get the LINEAR-ONLY part (transform the vector, transform the matrix's own origin, subtract — strips translation, keeps rotate/scale/skew, per the inline comment at 1351-1352). No other field (fillColor, strokeColor, strokeWidth, opacity, closed, any brush/text tag) is read or written by this function's vector branch at all.

packets.signature: function dupMatrixFromDescriptor(m,pivot){ var rad=(m.rot||0)*Math.PI/180,cs=Math.cos(rad),sn=Math.sin(rad); var a=cs*m.sx,b=sn*m.sx,c=-sn*m.sy,d=cs*m.sy; var tx=pivot.x+(m.dx||0)-a*pivot.x-c*pivot.y; var ty=pivot.y+(m.dy||0)-b*pivot.x-d*pivot.y; return new Matrix(a,b,c,d,tx,ty); }
packets.responsibility: Builds ONE closed-form affine — rotate+non-uniform-scale in the pivot's own local frame, translate LAST — from a placement DESCRIPTOR `m` (`{rot,sx,sy,dx,dy}`, the duplicator's per-clone placement shape produced by `_duplicatorClonePlacement`, C21g territory, cited by name only) and a world-space `pivot` point. Per CLAUDE.md §8 point 2 (cited by name only, documented in full in packet 5's own header comment at lines 1367-1373, NOT in this packet's own range — see this artifact's `boundaries`): built as a SINGLE expression rather than chained `Matrix.translate/rotate/scale` calls, because a bare paper.Matrix's own chained methods APPEND (compose in the opposite order Item.rotate/scale/translate would) — this closed-form is the 'fourth mirror' of the same algebra as affineFromMotion (engine-bridge.js), transformSegments (motion.js) and camera.js's own matrix build, all cited by name only, not re-mapped. Math: `a=cos(rad)·sx, b=sin(rad)·sx, c=-sin(rad)·sy, d=cos(rad)·sy` is the standard rotation×non-uniform-scale composition (R·S); `tx`/`ty` are solved so that `pivot` itself maps to `pivot+(dx,dy)` — i.e. the pivot is the fixed point of the rotate/scale part, and the placement's own `dx`/`dy` offset is added on top, last, in world space.

packets.responsibility: Computes an ANCHOR-POINT bounds center of a set of raw stroke dicts, for use as a pivot (not a render bound) — per its own comment, segment anchor points are precise enough for a pivot, so no bezier-extrema math and no throwaway Paper Path is built. Per-stroke handling: a raster stroke (`sd.isRaster`) contributes its own x±width/2 / y±height/2 rect to the running min/max, then `return`s (skips the segments check below, since a raster has no `segments` field at all — same schema fact packet 4 documents). A vector stroke with NO `segments` field is SKIPPED ENTIRELY via `if(!sd.segments)return;` — contributes nothing to the bounds (this is the one EXCLUSION: any stroke dict that is neither a raster nor carries segments, e.g. a malformed or future stroke-dict shape, is silently invisible to this pivot calculation). A vector stroke WITH segments contributes only each segment's own anchor `point` — handleIn/handleOut bezier control points are NEVER consulted, so a shape with a control handle extending far outside its anchor points' own bounding box will still pivot around the ANCHOR bounds, not the true rendered bounds. If no stroke contributed anything at all (`minX===Infinity`, i.e. `strokes` was empty or every entry was skipped), falls back to the CANVAS center (`state.canvasW/2, state.canvasH/2`) rather than an origin or NaN.

future_proposals: `effectorChannels`' one-time migration (app.js:1384-1393) never deletes the legacy `offsetPos`/`offsetRot`/`offsetScale`/`offsetOpacity` fields from `eff` after folding them into `eff.channels` — both the old and new shapes coexist on a migrated effector indefinitely. Not a correctness bug (nothing in this scope reads the legacy fields once `eff.channels` is truthy), but a minor persisted-size/clarity issue worth a follow-up cleanup pass; not changed here (out of this census's write scope).

`applyMatrixToStrokeData`'s raster branch (app.js:1330-1345) builds a FRESH literal listing only isRaster/src/x/y/width/height/opacity, silently DROPPING every other optional raster tag the input `sd` might carry (isBitmapBrush, linked/linkedPath/linkedHandleId, rotation, brushGroupId, isBrushTextureCopy, meshId, groupId, any text-tool field). Every confirmed caller in this scope (duplicator pool members, Component camera/symMatrix baking, StoryBoard's mirror) happens to operate on plain imported rasters/video frames in practice, so this has not been observed to lose a tag live — but a future caller applying this function to a linked-media or image-mesh raster would silently strip the `linked`/`meshId` tag from the CLONE it returns (the original `sd` passed to cloneStrokeForTransform is unaffected, only the transformed copy loses the tag). Worth either extending the raster branch's return literal or documenting the restriction explicitly; not changed here.

`_boundsCenterOfStrokes` uses ANCHOR points only, never handleIn/handleOut bezier control points — correct for its own stated purpose (a pivot, not a render bound) but means a shape whose curve bulges far outside its own anchor points' bounding box (e.g. a near-circular path built from 4 anchors with long handles) will pivot around a point that can be visibly offset from where the shape LOOKS centered. Flagged as an inherent approximation of the documented design, not a bug; not changed here.

The issue's own prompt hints at checking `transplant.js` as a possible `_HEAVY_STROKE_FIELDS` reader; direct grep confirms it is NOT — transplant.js copies whole stroke dicts via its own generic `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`, so a transplanted raster's `src`/`bitmapPressureProfile` round-trips through JSON like every other field, at whatever cost that implies for a large project. Not a bug (transplant is a one-shot, user-initiated action, not a per-frame/per-scrub hot path this scope's own 1.9ms measurement was about) but worth noting if transplant's own performance is ever profiled.
